title: Claude Wrote 90 Percent of Anthropic's Code - What That Means for Your Career
content:
More than 90% of the code at Anthropic last month was written by AI. And they still hired more engineers.
This comes from Anthropic's IPO filing, made public on October 26.
The company says over 90% of contributions to its codebase in September were written by Claude.
It also says the daily volume of code per engineer in the third quarter was more than 45 TIMES the average in 2024.
So did the engineers lose their jobs? No.
Anthropic had about 940 employees at the end of 2024. By September 30 this year, it had about 5,300.
The filing says its engineers increasingly direct and review Claude's work, rather than write code line by line.
One caution. This is a sales document from the company that sells the tool. And more code does not always mean more finished work.
But the direction is clear.
The job is shifting from typing code to 3 things.
1. Defining the problem clearly. An AI agent is only as good as the instructions you give it.
2. Reviewing. You need to spot the bug, the security hole, and the wrong assumption in code you did not write.
3. Owning the outcome. Someone still has to make sure the system works for the customer.
Say you are a junior developer, 2 years into your career.
Spend one hour a day giving a coding agent a real task, then review every line it writes.
In 6 months, you will think like a reviewer, and that is the skill teams are hiring for.
Here's my take.
AI is not removing the need for engineers. It is removing the need for ENGINEERS WHO ONLY TYPE.
Become the person who can direct the agent and check its work.
That skill is easy to practise. Pick any small project this week, let the agent write it, and then read every change before you accept it.
In my view, your judgment is the part that still matters most.
